summary: Ephemeral SA provisioning fails: credential name Unicode normalization mismatch across account bridge
summary_extended: Automated ephemeral service-account provisioning (ephemeral-ops-runner) intermittently fails during Dedicated onboarding flows. Root cause appears to be inconsistent Unicode normalization (NFC vs NFD) applied to service-account display names and generated session tags in the cross-cloud credential bridge, causing ARN/session-string mismatches and STS AssumeRole refusals.
impact: Provisioning of ephemeral service accounts for CI/LLM debug runners is blocked for multiple onboarding jobs. Several Dedicated tenant onboards are delayed; customer-facing provisioning flows timeout after retries. No data exfiltration observed but high-impact for time-sensitive debugging workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger ephemeral service-account provisioning via infra-onboard job (dedicated-provisioner) for project containing Unicode in display name (e.g., 'tested–node' where the dash is U+2013 EN DASH).
Observe provisioner logs: conformance layer creates GCP SA with name normalized to NFC but downstream bridge encodes role session name using NFD-normalized bytes.
Provisioner attempts AWS STS:AssumeRole with session tags that include the original display name; AWS returns AccessDenied with message 'Session tag mismatch for principalARN'.
Repeat with ASCII-only display name and flow succeeds deterministically.
Run uname -a and locale on provisioner pod — not needed for success reproduction but used to correlate container locale normalization behaviour.
logs: 2026-03-09T15:42:07Z provisioner: created GCP SA 'ephemeral-ops-测试' (name bytes NFC: 测试)
2026-03-09T15:42:09Z bridge: serializing session tags: role_session_name=ephemeral-ops-测试 (NFD bytes: 测试 but represented differently)
2026-03-09T15:42:09Z aws-sts: AssumeRole denied; error=AccessDenied, message=Session tag principal mismatch: expected 'ephemeral-ops-测试' got 'ephemeral-ops-测试'
2026-03-09T15:42:40Z prow-job: timeout after 3 retries; onboard job failed
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: role/session tag truncation or UTF-8 vs UTF-16 encoding mismatch. Collected logs from provisioner, bridge, and aws-sts components.

Reproduced locally against staging bridge when injecting a display name with combining diacritics (U+0301). Observed two code paths calling normalization: one uses Python's unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s) and the other uses Go's string bytes without explicit normalization (effectively NFD on some inputs).

Confirmed that AWS STS evaluates session tags using exact byte sequence of the session name when mapped to role session identifiers; mismatch causes AssumeRole rejection due to policy that binds tags to role session name.
GCP SA creation uses the display name as provided; internal canonicalizer normalizes to NFC in some code paths (not consistent).
Related flaky tickets: INT-342901 (env-tag-loss during cross-account impersonation) — similar surface but different root cause; linking for context.
temporary_workaround: Sanitize display names by stripping or ASCII-izing non-ASCII characters at the provisioner layer before calling the bridge. A short-lived patch added to staging deployment (tag: staging/ephemeral-provisioner@unicode-sanitize) which reduced failures for onboarding jobs using non-ASCII names.
recommended_fix: Standardize Unicode normalization across all components that participate in cross-cloud credential flows. Implement explicit NFC normalization in the bridge and the provisioner before creating role/session strings. Add unit tests asserting normalization for a set of canonical Unicode test vectors. Update role-session tag matching logic to compare normalized forms rather than raw bytes.
risk_and_rollout_notes: Normalization change is low-risk for ASCII-only tenants but touches auth/STS strings — will be rolled out to staging first with traffic shadowing, then to prod with a 1-hour canary. Add a feature flag to revert quickly. Coordinate with Security for audit of session-string canonicalization.
resolution: In progress — patch prepared (go:bridge#627) to enforce NFC; awaiting code review and end-to-end staging validation. Workaround remains in place for urgent onboards.
next_steps: 1) Ship NFC normalization patch to bridge (PR #627) and run e2e test against staging with non-ASCII display names.
2) Extend unit tests for provisioner and bridge with Unicode vectors (combining marks, composed vs decomposed).
3) After successful staging smoke tests, promote to prod behind feature flag and enable a 1-hour canary window.
4) Notify CS and Onboarding teams of change window and provide workaround guidance until fully rolled out.
